scenes.text: One man hiccuped for sixty-eight years straight.
His name was Charles Osborne, and it started in nineteen twenty-two on a farm in Nebraska.
He was hanging a hog for butchering when he fell, and the hiccups began.
On average, he hiccuped twenty to forty times a minute.
That adds up to an estimated four hundred and thirty million hiccups.
Then, in nineteen ninety, they simply stopped, and nobody knows why.
So what actually is a hiccup?
Your diaphragm, the big muscle under your lungs, suddenly jerks down.
Air rushes in, and your vocal cords snap shut. That snap is the hic.
Overeating, fizzy drinks, swallowing air and excitement can all set them off.
Even babies hiccup in the womb, long before they're born.
One idea says hiccups are a leftover from our fishy ancestors, who closed their throats to push water over their gills.
Another says they may help newborns avoid choking on milk.
But scientists still aren't sure why we hiccup at all.
And most home cures, like scares or holding your breath, have no solid evidence behind them.
What's your go-to hiccup cure? Tell me below.

title: This man had the hiccups for 68 years 😮
caption: Charles Osborne started hiccuping in 1922 and didn't stop until 1990, an estimated 430 million hiccups. Here's what a hiccup actually is.
